headline: ONE AGENCY SAYS CREATOR-SHOT FOOTAGE BEATS ITS OWN PROFESSIONALLY PRODUCED ADS BY 40 TO 60 PERCENT ONCE IT RUNS AS PAID ADVERTISING, SO IT HAS STARTED TRYING TO BUY THE FOOTAGE RIGHTS RATHER THAN THE POST
deck: Digiday published its annual agency survey this morning.  One named agency president in it describes what he thinks he is actually buying from a creator, and it is not a post on their channel.  It is the file, and permission to spend money pushing it.
tldr: An agency president told Digiday this morning that creator-shot footage run as paid advertising beats his agency's own produced creative by 40 to 60 percent, and that he is buying distribution rights on that footage in as many deals as he can.  Pull your three most recent creator contracts, find the clause covering paid use of the footage, and add duration, platforms and brand-account permission to your template this week.

Only about a third of agencies say client budgets grew, yet 78 percent are increasing creator spend and 89 percent are increasing streaming and television-screen video, while 60 percent are cutting billboards and 60 percent are cutting broadcast.  Write your next creator proposal with a named line for what it replaces, and ask the client which media contracts come up for renewal in the next two quarters.

A bundled creator deal can put as little as 35 percent of the budget in front of the creators themselves, against about 60 percent when the same work is billed line by line, and only 42 percent of UK marketers say they can see their creator agency fees in full.  Require every bidder to state talent share as a percentage on the first page of your next brief, and compare the bids on that figure as well as the total.

YouTube said on Thursday it will reduce Shorts distribution for channels re-uploading other creators' videos without adding value, naming narration over footage, minor technical edits and template-based bulk changes as things that do not count, and said nothing about channels cutting Shorts from their own long-form.  Mark your last twenty Shorts as template cut-downs or separate edits, and give every one in the first pile an element that exists only in that cut.

Selling AI-made creator-style video is the fashionable pitch at Advertising Week while a Shoptalk panel reported this morning had teenagers calling AI advertising a turnoff, one of them objecting that the saving came out of a designer's income rather than that the work looked fake.  Write down your disclosure rule for AI-made creator-style video this week, and put the budget into fewer creators kept for longer rather than synthetic volume.

The largest live audience on YouTube in September was Nintendo's own channel at 1.66 million people at once, about ten times the biggest individual streamer's peak of 162,700, while on hours watched an individual streamer beat every brand channel.  Ask for peak concurrents, average concurrents and hours watched together on every livestream plan, and if the brief is one big moment, announce a date three weeks out and stream once.

Hoka is buying the four weeks before the New York Marathon rather than race day, using six creators and digital billboards that score the boroughs against each other from a sponsored Strava challenge, so the creative refreshes daily from the runners' own logged mileage.  Map the four weeks before the one date your category always buys, and build creative that updates from something your audience already logs.
